resources.string: Pick a series of night-sky photos shot from a tripod (camera did not move between shots). Stars are aligned to the first frame; the ground (which does not move) is stacked separately, without alignment. At least 2 frames are required; for a visible improvement, 10-15 or more.
Some frames could not be aligned (too few shared stars) and were left out of the stack.
Mountains, trees and other objects are stacked separately (they do not move); the sky comes from all frames aligned on the stars.
Saved to Pictures/AstroStacker (TIFF goes to Download/AstroStacker if the gallery does not accept it)
Too few frames were successfully aligned (need at least 2). Check that the frames are from the same series with matching framing.
More than %1$d frames per series is not recommended: the sky rotates too far and artifacts appear near the edges. Split the shoot into several series.
Shot on location with the same camera and ISO. They remove electronic noise, hot pixels and vignetting, so more detail and color can be pulled from the result.
Lens cap on, same exposure and ISO as the light frames. 10–20 frames, right after the session (same sensor temperature).
Lens cap on, shortest exposure, same ISO. Removes the sensor offset. 20–30 frames.
Evenly lit lens (white phone screen or dawn sky through white cloth), same aperture and focus. Removes vignetting and dust. 10–20 frames.
Drag the corners to crop; drag inside the frame to move it. When you tilt the horizon, the frame shrinks automatically so no black corners appear.
Lossless, 16 bits per channel: the most data for editing in Photoshop, Lightroom, PixInsight. Large file; not every gallery app shows it.
Lossless, 8 bits per channel. Opens everywhere.
Maximum quality (100), 8 bits. Smallest file, for sharing.

Landscape shots from the same tripod without moving the camera, e.g. with a longer exposure or lower ISO for a clean foreground. If none are selected, the ground is stacked from the first 5 frames of the series.
Ground: stack of %1$d series frames, not aligned on stars
Ground: stack of %1$d separate ground shots
Pick 2 or more photos taken around one point with 20–30% overlap between neighbours. Order does not matter, and several rows (up/down) are fine — the app figures out how they fit together.

• Rotate the camera around the lens, not around yourself — otherwise nearby objects shift at the seams (parallax). A tripod is best.
• 25–30% overlap with the neighbouring frame; for several rows, a third vertically too.
• Manual exposure, white balance and focus — the same for all frames.
• Do not change zoom between frames. Moving people and cars at the seams may double.
Photos with no overlap with the rest: %1$d — left out.
Flat keeps straight lines straight (up to ~90°). Cylinder suits wide horizontal panoramas up to 360°. Sphere suits several rows and large vertical coverage.
Removes the uneven black border — keeps the largest rectangle without gaps.
